_comment: Broker licences: the information tiers of GDD 5.3, and the game's real
progression axis (Pillar 3). Capital is not the axis - a rich broker with
poor information should lose to a poorer one who can see further.
Tiers are cumulative and bought in order: holding one means holding every
tier beneath it. Each unlocks instrument classes to trade and research, and
names the Mytherra VisibilityScope it corresponds to.
About those scopes, honestly: the spectator projection this game reads
already carries every scope, so a licence cannot make the exchange unsee
what the server sent. The gate is the exchange's own - it decides what a
broker of this rank is shown and permitted to trade. The scopes are named
anyway because they are the vocabulary the tiers were designed against, and
because a Solo world source would be able to enforce them for real.
Every listing class must appear under exactly one tier, or paper would exist
that no licence could ever reach.
Costs rise far faster than the classes they unlock are worth, which is the
point: buying sight is meant to hurt.

tiers.blurb: Grain, ore and the tolls on the roads between. You may not ask whose roads.
